name: Motion
tagline: AI calendar and task scheduler that auto-plans your workday

pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 references list Individual at $34/month monthly and lower annual pricing.

verdictSummary: You can build an auto-scheduler for your own tasks, but robust calendar conflict handling, integrations, and productized rescheduling take real engineering.
coreLoopDIY: Create tasks with duration/deadline/priority, read calendar availability, solve a schedule, and write time blocks back.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the calendar stays organized without manual drag-and-drop.

priorArt.name: No maintained direct clone found
priorArt.desc: There are scheduling libraries, but no obvious maintained open-source Motion-equivalent co

notes: A good 'kinda' because the core algorithm is doable but the product promise is ongoing automation.
prompt:
Build me a personal replacement for Motion (AI calendar and task scheduler that auto-plans your workday). Requirements:

- Core loop: Create tasks with duration/deadline/priority, read calendar availability, solve a schedule, and write time blocks back.
- Needs: Google/Microsoft calendar OAuth.
- Needs: scheduling algorithm.
- Needs: hosted backend.
- Needs: notifications.
- Needs: task database.
- Keep it personal-scale: no accounts, no telemetry, secrets in .env, SQLite or
  flat files for storage. Local-first wherever possible.
- Clean minimal UI where one is needed; CLI is fine where one is not.
- Include a README with setup steps, required keys, and any OS permissions.

Honest scope: this covers the core loop only. You will not get: multi-calendar sync; recurring work rules; mobile apps.
